{"data":{"id":"475709046806","type":"page","title":"SSO Troubleshooting","status":"current","spaceId":"4708335613","snapshotToken":"v:1","detail":"full","body":{"format":"markdown","value":"This is meant to be a guide to help include or exclude SSO as a possible issue on your ticket.  This article is assuming that SSO has already been setup and in use.  If you are looking for how to configure SSO please refer to article 

<https://trebuco.atlassian.net/wiki/x/nxETRg> 

The two common issues I have seen recently is

1. User cannot access Search results in Secure
2. Cannot access a location(s) in Secure

Both of these have the same troubleshooting steps, but we have to do our research first.

1. Verify they are using SSO
    1. You can do that by going into the Waffle Menu-Settings-SSO+
2. Is the user in question listed in SSO+?
    1. Sometimes a client will have the user in the ‘Users’ section but you do not see them in the SSO+ section
3. Is the permissions/locations match in the User Profile and in the SSO+ profile? (screenshots below)
    1. This step tells us the most because if the user is not assigned in the SSO master file correctly then these two profiles will not match
4. The user having the issue; are they signed into a VPN?
    1. No VPN will equal no access




Possible Resolutions

The main communication I have sent to clients is educating them on why a permission is not there and what the next steps are.  This communication will wrap up all four of the steps I listed above.

*“The permission/location that this user is missing is not showing in the SSO permissions.  Whatever permissions/locations that are in the master file is what gets transmitted over to Secure.  Your IT Team should have access to the master file and as long as they add that permission/location then it will be transmitted to Secure.  If you would like to get on a phone call with your IT team we can arrange that to get this resolved.”*


Helpful information

1. Remember that the permissions/locations in SSO+ will override what is in the User Field.  That is important because Admins will add permissions into the User Section and sometimes that will work, but once the SSO file gets transmitted again it will remove that manual addition.

# 1. Overview

Secure Incident is a module available for clients who which to pay for it in Secure. Within Arpfiles, you may see it called by a couple different names: **Incident, LPMS, Audit**, **LPCase** and **Appriss Case**. In general, **Appriss Case** is the parent module and **Audit **and **Incident** can be enabled within **Appriss Case**. 

Secure Incident can be auto-enabled when creating a new client by including the flag `--lpcase true` in the template command. This will create the required `secure_Repo` and `seed-manifest` configurations so that Incident can be accessed via Secure. 

You may have to work the Incident team to make sure everything is configured correctly. Steve Procenko and  Jacob Tabbert both work on setting up new clients in Incident and are great resources.

In this article you will learn how to set up Secure Incident for a customer.

# 2. Prerequisites

Most prerequisites for Secure Incident are related to the Incident side, rather than Secure. However, if the client uses SSO to login to Secure and would like to use SSO for Incident, some additional information is needed.

#### 2.1. LPMS database region:

- This will match the ARDM database region and will be created when running the template with `--lpcase true` .

#### 2.2. LPMS SSO:

- To test SSO successfully the location hierarchy needs to be created and users need to be assigned to at least one store. Any user who uses LPMS will also need to have the correct permissions.

# 3. Important notice

Setting up Universal SSO for LPMS is a common request. Please make sure the location hierachy has been created, users have access to at least one store, and users have the proper permissions before testing with the client. It may be hard or impossible to test with your own account as you may not have access to Incident. Working closely with one of the Incident experts (Steve Procenko or Jacob Tabbert) will make the setup process go smoothly.

```
--lpcase true
```

Replace `hottopic` with your client name. You may have to reach out to the audit team to get the url.
